newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dassault in govt talks on Rafale funding.
newsitem.headline: Dassault in govt talks on Rafale funding.

text.p: French combat plane maker Dassault Aviation is in talks with the government over who will pay an estimated 700 million francs in interest charges on a proposed bank loan to fund an early batch of Rafale jets, Dassault executives said on Friday.

Dassault, along with three companies building the main Rafale systems, want to bring forward the delivery of a half-squadron of 10 Rafales to the year 2001 from 2005 for the French air force, to help its export sales.
Bank funding for the planes is estimated at three to four billion francs, according to a parliamentary report.
Lagardere's Matra supplies the Rafale's Mica and Magic missiles, Thomson-CSF the advanced RBE2 radar and Snecma the M88-2 motors.

A Dassault executive said a compromise would probably be found on the interest financing. The companies, which would raise the loan on their own balance sheets, are keen to reach an agreement on the interest payments by the end of the year.
The companies already finance 25 percent of the Rafale's development from their own funds.

Dassault is keen to have the 10 Rafales flying with the French air force earlier than the year 2005, envisaged by the six-year defence budget law, as this would help its sales drive to the United Arab Emirates.
